tags: @guarantee ok.zero-limit-blocks-all Setting `limit` to 0 blocks all requests instead of disabling the rate limiter.
@guarantee ok.default-message `message` defaults to "Too many requests, please try again later.".

@guarantee ok.default-legacy-headers `legacyHeaders` defaults to true, which sends the "X-RateLimit-Limit", "X-RateLimit-Remaining" and (if the store provides it) "X-RateLimit-Reset" headers on all responses.
@guarantee ok.default-request-property-name `requestPropertyName` defaults to "rateLimit", the name of the property on the request that holds the rate limit info.
@guarantee ok.ipv4-unchanged An IPv4 address is returned unchanged.
@guarantee ok.default-ipv6-subnet-56 When `ipv6Subnet` is not given it defaults to 56, so an IPv6 address is returned as the network address of its /56 subnet in CIDR notation.
@guarantee ok.ipv6-subnet-false With `ipv6Subnet` set to `false`, an IPv6 address is also returned unchanged.
@guarantee ok.ipv4-mapped-ipv6 An IPv4-mapped IPv6 address (the "::ffff:0:0/96" range) is returned as the IPv4 address it contains, whichever notation it arrives in.
@guarantee ok.second-ms `SECOND` is one second in milliseconds, usable for `windowMs`.
@guarantee ok.minute-ms `MINUTE` is 60000, a duration in milliseconds (1 minute, the default `windowMs`).
@guarantee ok.hour-ms `HOUR` is one hour in milliseconds, so `3 * HOUR` is a 3 hour `windowMs`.
@guarantee ok.day-ms `DAY` is one day in milliseconds.
